subject: gk
question: Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:**Statement 1:** Rural-to-urban migration is a major contributor to urban growth in India.**Statement 2:** Better job opportunities and education facilities in cities attract migrants.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rural-to-urban migration** is characterized by the movement of people from villages to cities in search of better living conditions. In **India**, this process has been a fundamental driver of **urbanization** and the expansion of metropolitan boundaries. According to the **2011 Census**, the urban population grew by **91 million** in a decade, with a significant portion attributed to migration and the reclassification of rural areas into **Census Towns**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The primary drivers of this migration are known as **pull factors**, which include the availability of **stable employment** in the industrial and service sectors. Urban centers like **Mumbai**, **Delhi**, and **Bengaluru** offer a diverse range of **job opportunities** that are often absent in the agricultural-dependent rural economy. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Beyond employment, **educational facilities** act as a major magnet. Cities house premier institutions such as **IITs**, **AIIMS**, and major **Central Universities**, attracting students from rural regions seeking quality higher education and specialized training.
 
• Migration in **India** is often motivated by the "urban wage premium," where **numerical values** of daily wages in urban informal or formal sectors significantly exceed those in rural farm labor. This economic disparity encourages the **labor force** to shift towards cities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Push and Pull Factors:** **Push factors** are negative conditions in rural areas like **poverty**, lack of **healthcare**, and **agricultural distress** that force people to leave. **Pull factors** are positive attractions in cities like **modern infrastructure**, **better communication**, and **entertainment** facilities.
 
• **Internal Migration Trends:** In **India**, **female migration** is predominantly due to **marriage**, whereas **male migration** is primarily driven by **work and business**. The **Economic Survey 2016-17** highlighted that the annual interstate migration in **India** was close to **9 million** between **2011 and 2016**.
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:** **Article 19(1)(d)** and **Article 19(1)(e)** of the **Constitution of India** grant citizens the fundamental right to **move freely** throughout the territory of **India** and to **reside and settle** in any part of the country.
 
• **Impact of Urbanization:** While migration aids **economic growth** and increases the **GDP**, it also puts pressure on **urban infrastructure**, leading to the growth of **slums**, increased **pollution**, and challenges in **waste management**.
 
• **Government Initiatives:** To manage urban growth and migration, the **Government of India** has launched schemes like **AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation)**, **Smart Cities Mission**, and **PMAY-U (Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban)** to provide **affordable housing** and **basic amenities** to migrants and urban dwellers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Census 2011 Data:** The **level of urbanization** in **India** increased from **27.81%** in **2001** to **31.16%** in **2011**. The total number of **migrants** in **India** was **45.36 crore**, making up nearly **38%** of the total population.
 
• **Economic Impact:** Migrants contribute significantly to the **remittance economy**, sending money back to rural households, which helps in **poverty alleviation** and improving the **standard of living** in villages.
</ul
